cash_breakdown.item: Bank deposits with original maturity over three months
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Mainly group/PRC bank deposits, not shown as restricted, but only RMB 61.357m cash sits at the listed company; term and cross-entity dividend/remittance uncertainty require mainland group-cash haircut.
cash_breakdown.reason: Potentially detachable without stopping operations after retaining short-term operating cash.

cash_breakdown.item: Financial assets at FVTPL - unquoted fund investment
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Unquoted fund investment; fair value exists but liquidity and redemption terms are not disclosed, so use non-listed fund low-end haircut.
cash_breakdown.reason: Possible non-operating investment asset, but not cash-equivalent.

cash_breakdown.item: Bank deposits with original maturity three months or less / cash equivalents
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Retained as necessary operating liquidity; amount roughly equals a conservative three-month cash operating-cost buffer for a cement producer in downturn.
cash_breakdown.reason: Needed to keep manufacturing, sales, payables and tax cycle running.

cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Government-regulated restricted bank accounts, bills-payable guarantee deposits and long-maturity security deposit are not detachable.
cash_breakdown.reason: Cannot be taken out without affecting regulatory/guarantee/security obligations.

cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Bank borrowings are unsecured RMB borrowings and deducted at 100%.
cash_breakdown.reason: External financing liability that must be repaid or assumed by a controller.

cash_breakdown.item: Tax, FX and dividend friction reserve
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Cash is mainly RMB group/PRC cash; 2024 filing separately records RMB241.601m deferred tax on undistributed PRC subsidiary earnings, supporting a reserve for extraction friction.
cash_breakdown.reason: Reserve for taxes, dividend remittance and execution friction after control acquisition.

cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Checked but not mechanically deducted from detachable net cash because leases are continuing operating leases for the business; their cash effect is reflected in cash-flow/profit quality.
cash_breakdown.reason: Continuing operations need the leased assets.

cash_breakdown.item: Bills payables paired with restricted guarantee deposits
cash_breakdown.haircut_reason: Supplier settlement bills are operating payables, and the paired guarantee deposit is already assigned zero detachable value; no extra financing deduction to avoid double counting.
cash_breakdown.reason: Operating settlement arrangement disclosed in note 28.

profit_quality.assessment: 2024 reported parent loss was RMB263.7m, but operating cash flow remained RMB459.7m and capex was RMB457.6m, leaving only RMB2.2m operating cash flow after capex. 2022-2023 were much stronger, so the main denominator uses the three-year average of operating cash flow less capex (RMB825.3m) and then applies a 0.30 haircut for cement-cycle downturn, 2024 loss, falling revenue and working-capital volatility.
adjustments: Use operating cash flow less purchase of property, plant and equipment as the pre-haircut distributable cash-profit proxy: 2022 RMB1.255bn, 2023 RMB1.219bn, 2024 RMB0.002bn.
Do not add back bank deposit interest as operating earnings; interest income is treated as non-core and cash assets are separately handled in detachable funds.
Do not use the best year or median FCF directly because 2024 revenue and profit collapsed and the cement industry is cyclical.
Use a 0.30 cash-profit haircut, within the “recent loss / weak cash flow” range, to turn historical cash conversion into a conservative sustainable distributable cash estimate.
profit_quality.cashflow_support: Three-year operating cash flow less capex: 2022 RMB1.255bn, 2023 RMB1.219bn, 2024 RMB0.002bn. Average RMB825.3m; discounted at 0.30 to RMB247.6m.
profit_quality.haircut_reason: Latest year turned loss and free cash after capex was near zero; cement price/demand cycle and working-capital swings make historical cash profit only partially distributable.
profit_quality.cash_conversion_assessment: Historical cash conversion is good in 2022-2023, but 2024 is effectively breakeven after capex. The main issue is sustainability, not accounting cash conversion alone.
profit_quality.maintenance_capex_assessment: Maintenance capex is not separately disclosed; purchase of property, plant and equipment is used as a conservative proxy.
profit_quality.working_capital_assessment: Working capital has released cash in prior years but 2024 includes a large increase in restricted bank deposits. No standalone normal reinvestment amount is disclosed; handled through OCF and profit haircut.

evidence.note: Input labels currency as CNY; treated as RMB/CNY equivalent for formula.
Includes RMB7.589bn deposits over three months and RMB1.295bn three months or less.

Unsecured and unguaranteed RMB bank borrowings.
Supports applying group/PRC cash haircut rather than listed-parent cash treatment.

evidence.metric: three-year operating cash flow less capex
evidence.source: 2024, 2023 and 2022 annual report cash flow statements

limitations: The annual report does not split group bank balances by listed parent, offshore subsidiaries and PRC operating subsidiaries beyond the company-only balance sheet; owner-earnback cash haircut therefore uses a mainland/group-cash discount.
The term profile beyond “original maturity over three months” is not disclosed; the main haircut assumes deposits are bank deposits but not immediately parent-level distributable cash.
Maintenance capex is not separately disclosed from growth capex; owner-earnback uses purchase of property, plant and equipment as a conservative capex proxy.

No exact normal working-capital reinvestment estimate is disclosed; operating cash flow already includes annual working-capital movements, so the profit denominator is additionally haircut rather than double-deducting an arbitrary amount.
Market cap is the runner input historical CNY estimate rather than an independently recomputed current quote.

Negative operating-business price means the discounted detachable net cash exceeds the input market cap; the formula therefore yields a negative earnback year count, economically meaning cash coverage exceeds purchase price under the chosen haircuts.
This is a control-acquisition cash-flow analysis only, not an investment recommendation or target price.
